newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Corpoven to raise output potential 56 pct by 2006.
newsitem.headline: Corpoven to raise output potential 56 pct by 2006.

text.p: Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) unit Corpoven aims to raise its output potential by 56 percent to 1.63 million barrels per day (bpd) by 2006, Corpoven President Guillermo Archila said.
Heavy and extra heavy crudes are seen taking a larger share of this potential output, growing from 166,000 bpd at present to 384,000 bpd in 2006, Archila was quoted as saying in a company release.

Corpoven has signed a $3.5 billion joint venture deal with Atlantic Richfield Co Texaco Inc and Phillips Petroleum Co to produce up to 200,000 barrels per day of nine-degree API extra-heavy crude oil from the Hamaca zone in Venezuela's Orinoco tar belt.
Natural gas production will also more than double to 6.650 billion cubic feet in 2006, compared to 3.080 billion cubic feet at present, he added.
By 2006 Corpoven expects to be making an annual net profit of $2.410 billion, up from $660 million expected for 1996, Archila added.

Corpoven is one of three main PDVSA subsidiaries engaged in exploration, production and refining. PDVSA officials have said they expect to raise Venezuela's crude production potential from 3.2 million bpd to close to six million bpd over the next decade.
